newsitem.title: CHILE: U.S. TO PROPOSE "FAST-TRACK" BILL SEPTEMBER 10.
newsitem.headline: U.S. TO PROPOSE "FAST-TRACK" BILL SEPTEMBER 10.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton will send new "fast track" trade negotiation legislation to Congress on September 10, said U.S ambassador in Santiago Gabriel Guerra-Mondragon.
"President Clinton will introduce the fast track law on September 10," Guerra-Mondragon told reporters.
Guerra-Mondragon said a group of U.S. congressmen would visit Chile this week to see the country before the debate on fast-track powers begins in Washington.
Fast-track legislation allow U.S. negotiators to agree trade accords which Congress can then only accept or reject without the power to make changes.
Talks on Chile's bid to join the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) stalled last year after discussion on "fast-track" powers died in Congress.

Chilean officials have said they will only hold talks with U.S. representatives if they have fast track powers, as Chileans fear that otherwise any agreement would be picked apart by Congress under the influence of special interest groups.
